fix_draft: microcosm issue (link from PolicyEngine/microcosm#646): 'Pooled ASEC income years enter the US H5 at nominal own-year dollars; SPM poverty tests them against 2024 thresholds'. Cite the doc lines, the income/SPM_TOTVAL ratios (~1.000 every year) and threshold ratios (1.137/1.058/1.004), and the counterfactual (national child -2.59 pp, total -1.58 pp). Note that a pool whose mean income year equals the target year (the new 2023-2025 default) still biases threshold-based rates. title: Thin state samples around a common national shift: the state gaps are within PE's own sampling error; no state-specific defect

split.construction_issue: the registry reports a 26-155-effective-household subgroup rate with no uncertainty, and the |ratio-1|>=50% queue rule selects on noise in low-rate states
split.pe_gap: data: sparse per-state sample; the populace weighting puts more child weight on Census-poor records than the CPS (Census SPM_POOR on populace weights 16.5% child / 14.0% total vs published 13.4% / 12.9%)

evidence: computed: queued child rows have Kish effective child households 26-149 (ME 26, RI 39, VT 42, NH 43, DE 45, NE 51, WV 55, WA 68, TN 74, UT 78, MA 83, VA 83, FL 149); the 10 largest households hold 15-48% of child weight; household-cluster linearized PE SEs 3.7-7.1 pp (OR total: 155, 11%, 3.0 pp)

computed: centred on the national bias (+2.43 pp child, +0.16 pp total), 12 of 14 high-side rows have |z|<2 (TN 2.14, FL 2.05); child chi2 99.4/50 incl. MT, 59.1/49 excl. MT (p=0.15); total chi2 78.7/50 (Census SE 0) and 51.7/50 (Census SE 1.5 pp); OR z=1.84

computed: weighting component (Census SPM_POOR on populace weights minus published) is +3.1 pp nationally (child) and consistent with noise across states (chi2 53.7/50, p=0.33); it is the largest component for RI (+11.2), VT (+9.3), VA (+10.4), FL (+13.3), OR total (+7.6), where the engine is below the Census flag on the same records (-0.9 to -3.6 pp)
computed: FL ASEC-channel children carry 39% of FL child weight with a Census SPM_POOR rate of 40.3% (populace weights) / 37.5% (A_FNLWGT): the sparse selection kept a very poor FL subset

registry: microcosm state_spm_poverty_levels.json:2 (comment: single-state gaps of a couple of points are noise; the systematic pattern is the signal); reform_validation.py:933-982 (_person_rate emits no SE)
data/populations.json: every high state except MT was also high under Build O (e.g. TN 19.1, DE 22.7, VT 19.7, VA 20.1)
fix_draft: (a) microcosm reform_validation.py _person_rate: emit the household-cluster linearized SE and the effective household count with each statistic='rate' row; the scorecard queues state rate rows on |z| (centred on the national gap) instead of |ratio-1|>=50%. (b) Annotation for these rows until then: 'PE's state SPM rate rests on about N effective households (PE SE about X pp). After the national shift tracked in #646, the gap is within sampling error; Census's own SPM flag on the same weighted records is Y%. Not a state-specific model defect.'

title: Montana child SPM 0.31x: three cloned source families on about 52 effective households; one is a Census negative-resources artifact

fix_draft: Annotation: 'Montana's PE child SPM rate (2.5%) rests on about 52 effective households. Three source families hold 14.75 pp of MT child weight.
